title.narrative: UNJP - SDG Business Partnerships and Solutions
UNJP - SDG Business Partnerships and Solutions

description.narrative:
The overall objective of this Project is to raise the awareness among private sector actors about SDGs and the ways businesses will benefit from them and contribute to their implementation in Albania. Indeed, in addition to offering a wealth of expertise and disruptive innovation, businesses can help mobilize much needed capital in support of the SDGs, while reorienting their strategies to create value not just for their shareholders, but society at large.
The main project objective will be achieved through two main Outcomes:
Outcome 1. Technical Capacity Companies are equipped with technical knowledge and skills to implement sustainable practices and move towards higher value added business models.
Outcome 2. Enabling Environment Companies are aware of sustainable practices, connected to academia and to national and international business opportunities to upgrade them as well as in active communication with policy makers while consumers increasingly value sustainability.

Att stödja albanska företag att implementera hållbara affärsmetoder som kommer att vara katalytiska för att göra det möjligt för den lokala privata sektorn att ha en positiv inverkan på albansk ekonomi, klimat och samhälle. De direkta förmånstagarna kommer att vara albanska företag, nämligen deras ägare och deras arbetskraft samt lokala och centrala statliga institutioner. Särskild uppmärksamhet kommer att ägnas åt att rikta in sig på kvinnor, ungdomar och utsatta grupper. Andra relevanta intressenter kommer att vara branschorganisationer, handelskamrar, internationella företag, universitet och finansiella institutioner.

To support Albanian companies in implementing sustainable business practices which will be catalytic in enabling the local private sector in having a positive impact on Albanian economy, climate and society.The direct beneficiaries will be Albanian companies, namely their owners and their workforce as well as local and central government institutions. Specific attention will be paid to targeting women, young people and vulnerable groups. Other relevant stakeholders will be sectoral associations, chambers of commerce, international companies, universities and financial institutions.

title.narrative: Amendment No 3 to the Standard Administrative Agreement on SDG Fund II Albania
Decision on Contribution for a UNJP on Business Partnerships and Solutions for SDG

description.narrative:
In 2025, the UN Joint Project Business Partnerships and Solutions for SDGs, phase II advanced Albanias transition toward a more sustainable, competitive and inclusive private sector by delivering integrated support across the agri food/ agroprocessing and textile, clothing, leather and footwear (TCLF) sectors.
During 2025 the implementation combined enterpriselevel technical assistance with business development and skills support, while reinforcing private sector awareness and engagement around the SDGs and EUaligned sustainability requirements, with the aim of achieving valuechainwide impact: as beneficiary companies become more competitive and adopt best practices, these improvements extend to their suppliers and customers through business linkages and market expectations.
- In the agri food and agroprocessing sector, the programme applied a value chainoriented approach to improve farm management practices, reduce environmental footprint, strengthen climate resilience and enhance competitiveness. At enterprise level, the Growing with Your Business (GyB) methodology generated measurable results for 12 agroprocessing SMEs in Lushnjë, including an average 20% increase in sales, 1740% growth in customers, improved compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and more than EUR 200,000 in own counter investment. A new GyB cycle was launched in Belsh, engaging 12 olive processing enterprises. In parallel, farmlevel upgrading was delivered through SDG Demonstration Farms and Farmer Field Schools, reaching more than 35 farmers across priority value chains. Three SDG Demonstration Farms (tomato, cucumber and olives) were established as practical learning hubs, supported by Farmer Field Schools that delivered 17 training days in 2025. To strengthen investment readiness and market integration, two bankable business model upgrades for greenhouse vegetable production (low and mediumtechnology models) were developed, with clearly defined investment and working capital requirements. At enterprise level, this was further supported through the application of the Resource Efficient and Cleaner Production (RECP) methodology, assisting 12 agroprocessing enterprises across subsectors including olive oil, meat processing, dairy and medicinal plants, with a focus on improved resource efficiency, reduced environmental footprint and alignment with EU sustainability requirements
- In the Textile Clothing Leather and Footwear (TCLF) sector, the project supported enterprises to improve productivity, working conditions and sustainability performance in a challenging market environment marked by reduced demand and financial pressure. More than 30 enterprises received direct technical and sustainability support, reaching approximately 1,200 workers (~90% of whom are women). The Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE) programme delivered strong enterpriselevel results, including average productivity gains of 42%, energy reductions of 20%, nearly 50% defect reduction, and improvements in occupational safety, worker engagement and retention. Resource Efficient and Cleaner Production (RECP) methodology implementation was scaled through assessments in 20 enterprises, identifying 65 concrete efficiency measures and demonstrating pathways to competitiveness through improved energy, water, and waste efficiency. Complementary actions supported upgrading beyond lowvalue cutmaketrim (CMT) production through CAD/CAM training, alongside strengthened occupational safety and health practices, including adaptation of the ILO OSH Code of Practice and training of labour inspectors. Moreover, UNIDO initiated a survey on resourceuse efficiency targeting at least 70 SMEs. The survey results will provide insights into the current situation and sector needs related to productivity and innovation. Together with RECP assessment findings, they will inform a planned analytical publication to be finalized and presented to a wider audience in spring 2026. More than 70% of the proposed measures are directly aligned with EU Green Deal objectives, confirming the strong relevance of the RECP approach in supporting Albanians industrial alignment with EU environmental and climate priorities.
- At ecosystem level, the project increased private sector engagement and awareness on sustainability and the SDGs through flagship events, assessments and communication products, with more than 350 companies participating in sustainabilityrelated activities, including sustainability assessments, the Business #2030 Conference and the SDG Business Pioneers Award. Evidence based policy dialogue was supported through enterprise surveys, sector mapping and environmental impact analysis, providing practical guidance aligned with EU accession priorities. Visibility and knowledge sharing were further enhanced through dedicated digital platforms, multimedia outputs, publications and case studies, positioning the project as a national reference for sustainable and inclusive private sector development
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
